item.text: {"decisions":[{"item_id":"feed:849c1b75f58f080d47c7e603","version_id":"4db87a90c2dc300949c1e3994c64751a7fc731fb9cc1ae42f2b1167e82b48dce","decision":"reject","reason":"The September 25 publication falls within September 11–October 10, but is a general AI resource directory rather than substantive new research evidence. Error checking and information seeking are relevant to desk research, yet the linked studies' methods, dates and supporting passages are absent. Their summaries cannot establish recent findings or small-business applicability; the guide supplies no new test or documented research workflow.","piece_ids":[]},{"item_id":"feed:95101d78a52e28ec8b595c3d","version_id":"0f7f600e63ed9452687f9f4e5647405b9bfcd0fb46a43c73993ffd9e5e75b472","decision":"reject","reason":"The September 14 article is timely but promotes a forthcoming MAICON session about general marketing automation and content strategy, without a concrete customer, competitor or market-research application. The attributed advice to test prompts is inspectable opinion, not evidence of effectiveness: no worked research example, evaluation, cost or results are supplied. The publisher's conference-registration incentive is explicit. It shares a publisher and promotional format with the Franco article, so these are not independent perspectives, although no exact cross-post is established.","piece_ids":[]},{"item_id":"feed:9b5446bea79d40805fc10d3e","version_id":"12085ef4368b03fd065341d410d51aefb0a32bdf79b2842509dee8208e25e1dc","decision":"reject","reason":"The October 5 article concerns earning brand visibility in AI recommendations, rather than using AI to gather or validate market evidence. It promotes MAICON and an agency executive's forthcoming session; both conference sales and agency positioning create commercial incentives. Claims about publishers influencing visibility rely on unavailable proprietary data, with no sample, model versions, comparison or evaluation method. It repeats the same publisher's conference-promotion format as the Crestodina article and provides no independent corroboration.","piece_ids":[]},{"item_id":"feed:aaa748520b768d551a2cc477","version_id":"60995190c3f305fd3305d2f89b47dd3c2a89f0a45024504014655bc8fa268e27","decision":"reject","reason":"The September 16 account is timely, but automating Keynote formatting from human-created research and scripts falls under excluded generic content creation, without demonstrating better research gathering, validation or synthesis. The practitioner account supports an attributed experience and a potentially useful token-cost constraint, but its '80%' completion estimate lacks a defined measure, baseline, timing or actual costs. The article explicitly repackages Episode 239, so that podcast would repeat the underlying claim rather than independently corroborate it. The publisher also promotes its commercial AI Academy.","piece_ids":[]}]}
